payload.headline: QQQ slips below its 200-day average; SPY holds long trend, breadth thin

summary.thesis: Tech (QQQ) is in a downtrend. It closed at 679.89, just under its 200-day average of 681.20 and well below its 50-day average of 717.72. The broad market (SPY) is moving sideways at 754.37: above its 200-day average of 729.32 but below its 50-day average of 764.09. Fear is normal, but only 27% of stocks are above their 50-day averages.
summary.decision: Long-term: stand aside. Swing: stand aside. The previous note said a QQQ close below its 200-day average would be a stand-aside signal, and that close happened today.
summary.act_at: A QQQ close above 681.20 ends the downtrend, per the market gate. That would support a selective stance again. A QQQ close above 717.72 would put tech's short-term trend back up and pass the pipeline's market check.

payload.happening: SPY closed at 754.37, down 0.36% from 757.12. QQQ fell further, down 1.2% to 679.89 from 688.17. Over five sessions both are still up: SPY 2.59% and QQQ 3.63%. That is a bounce from the Nov 5 lows of 733.0 for SPY and 647.05 for QQQ. Over 20 sessions both are down: SPY -1.16% and QQQ -4.21%. Both remain below their Oct 6 highest closes of the past year, 779.09 for SPY and 759.66 for QQQ. PPI producer-price data was scheduled for today at 08:30, but DATA contains no result for it and no news since the last note.
payload.business: Read together: (1) Trend. SPY's long trend holds, but its short trend is broken. QQQ is below both its 50- and 200-day averages, which counts as a downtrend. (2) Fear. The VIX was about 18.7 on Nov 12, in the 'normal' band (15–20), up from about 17.49 the day before. Its percentile reading is 71 over the past 252 days. The Nov 13 VIX reading isn't stored yet, so this is one day old. (3) Breadth. Only 27% of stocks are above their 50-day averages, so most stocks are in short-term downtrends even though SPY is near its 50-day average. Together: no panic, but tech has lost its long-term trend line and participation is narrow. In general terms (general knowledge), that pattern usually means a few large names are holding up the index.

worth.text: No valuation applies here. The levels below are price-trend markers, not estimates of fair value.
worth.key_assumption: No valuation is implied. The levels are price-trend markers only.

bull: QQQ is only 1.31 (0.19%) below its 200-day average of 681.20, so a small gain would end the downtrend per the market gate.
SPY is 3.3% above its 200-day average of 729.32, so the broad market's long-term trend still counts as up.
Both indices are up over five sessions (SPY 2.59%, QQQ 3.63%) from the Nov 5 lows, which are holding. The VIX is in the normal band, and DATA shows a 5-day change of -9.48.
bear: QQQ closed below its 200-day average of 681.20 and is 5.6% below its 50-day average of 717.72. Its trend is labeled a downtrend.
Breadth is weak: only 27% of stocks are above their 50-day averages.
QQQ fell 1.2% today and is down 4.21% over 20 sessions. SPY is still 1.3% below its 50-day average of 764.09 and 2.5% below its 1-month high of 773.09.

levels.what: QQQ 200-day average. A close above it ends the tech downtrend per the market gate and would support a selective stance again.
QQQ 50-day average. A close above it would put the short-term trend back up and pass the pipeline's market check. That would be the cue to lean in more.
QQQ 1-month high (Oct 28). A close above it would mean the tech pullback is fully recovered.
SPY 50-day average. A close above it would put SPY's short-term trend back up.
SPY 1-month high (Oct 21). A close above it would mean SPY's pullback is fully recovered.
SPY 1-month low (Nov 5). A close below it would set a new 1-month low, meaning the decline is continuing.
SPY 200-day average. A close below it would put the broad market's long-term trend down too.
QQQ 1-month low (Nov 5). A close below it would mean the tech decline is continuing.

longterm.why: The previous note named a QQQ close below its 200-day average as a stand-aside signal, and QQQ closed at 679.89 against 681.20. SPY's long trend and normal fear argue the damage is limited for now. But with tech in a downtrend and breadth at 27%, the readings don't support new buying until QQQ recovers 681.20.

swing.why: QQQ closed at 679.89, below its 50-day average of 717.72. Per the trend gates, setups keep failing the pipeline's market check until QQQ closes above that level.

decision.timing: PPI was scheduled for Nov 13 at 08:30 as an early read on inflation pressure. DATA reports no result. NVDA reports earnings on an estimated Nov 17, after the close. Per DATA, its big index weight means the report moves the whole tech group, and that comes with QQQ sitting right at its 200-day gate. The VIX reading is from Nov 12; the Nov 13 value isn't stored yet.

change_mind: A QQQ close above 681.20 (200-day average) ends the downtrend per the market gate. That would support moving back to selective. A further close above 717.72 (50-day average) would support leaning in more.
A SPY close below 733.0 (1-month low) or 729.32 (200-day average), or a QQQ close below 647.05 (1-month low), would mean the decline is spreading or continuing. That would reinforce standing aside.
payload.what_changed: QQQ closed at 679.89, down from 688.17. In the previous note QQQ was 1.1% above its 200-day average; it is now 0.2% below it. That flips the market gate to an active downtrend, so the long-term stance moves from selective to stand aside, and swing stays stand aside. Breadth edged up from 25% to 27%. The moving averages shifted: SPY 50-day from 764.43 to 764.09, SPY 200-day from 728.99 to 729.32, QQQ 50-day from 718.46 to 717.72, QQQ 200-day from 680.94 to 681.20. QQQ's 1-month high is now 725.61 (Oct 28), not 728.0 (Oct 15), because the 20-day window rolled forward. No news was reported since the last note.
